requirement:
The Python outline exposes the following items beneath its file root:

| Construct | Kind | Name |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Functions and methods | `def` | Declared name |
| Classes | `class` | Declared name |

Nested definitions appear beneath their nearest enclosing outline item.
Decorators attach to the definition they decorate and are included in its
selected source and structural hash.

Item selectors, percent encoding, anonymous identities, and duplicate-name
suffixes follow {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`.
rationale:
Obligations and the tests that cover them:

- **Functions and methods as `def`, named by declared name.** `python_profile_outlines_defs_classes_and_statements` in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs` asserts `def[f]` and the method `class[C]/def[m]`. `python_nested_definitions_use_the_nearest_outline_ancestor` in `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs` also covers `async def`.
- **Classes as `class`, named by declared name.** Both tests above assert `class[C]`, `class[Outer]` and `class[Outer]/class[Inner]`.
- **Nested definitions beneath the nearest enclosing outline item.** `python_nested_definitions_use_the_nearest_outline_ancestor` asserts the full selector list. It covers a class in a class, a def in a method that is nested in an `if`, a class in a def, a method in that class, and an async def in an async def. The `if` block is not an outline item, so `def[local]` correctly nests under `def[method]`.
- **Decorators in the selected source.** `python_selected_source_includes_its_decorators` asserts that the selected text of a decorated def equals the whole source and that the item span starts at 0. It also asserts that each of two decorated same-name classes starts with its own decorator. `python_nested_definitions_use_the_nearest_outline_ancestor` checks that a decorated method selects text starting with `@decorate`.
- **Decorators in the structural hash.** `python_decorators_attach_to_the_decorated_definition_for_hashing` asserts that changing or removing a decorator changes the def's hash, and that whitespace between the decorator and the def does not. It also asserts that a method's decorator changes the enclosing class's structural hash but not its identity hash. No test hashes a decorated class directly. The decorator is attached to the following item by the same Python `attachment_target` mechanism for defs and classes, so this class-only variant is not a distinct obligation.
- **Selector conventions** (percent encoding, anonymous identities, duplicate-name suffixes) are cited from `requirements.references.outline_selectors`. The duplicate-name case is applied to Python in the `class[Checked]#1` and `class[Checked]#2` selections. Percent encoding is generic and is tested in `selector.rs`. Python items always have names, so no anonymous items arise.

The assertions are specific and would catch wrong kinds, names, nesting or decorator handling. I found no adequacy gaps.

text: :::{req} items
The Python outline exposes the following items beneath its file root:
| Construct | Kind | Name |
| Functions and methods | `def` | Declared name |
| Classes | `class` | Declared name |
Nested definitions appear beneath their nearest enclosing outline item.
Decorators attach to the definition they decorate and are included in its
selected source and structural hash.
Item selectors, percent encoding, anonymous identities, and duplicate-name
suffixes follow {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`.
:::{req} outline_selectors
Habeas uses the TBV [outline selector grammar](sdk/outlines.md#parse-an-outline-selector)
under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax` for source addresses.
:::{req} selector_syntax
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. In a multipart label such as `impl[Thing/Trait]`, `/` separates
name parts. A slash within one part is encoded as `%2F`. Line numbers MUST NOT
form part of a selector.
